chunks.title: Faraday's Law of Induction
Lenz's Law
Eddy Currents

questions: State Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction and write the formula for induced EMF in a coil of N turns.
A circular coil of 200 turns and radius 10 cm is placed perpendicular to a magnetic field changing at 0.5 T/s. Calculate the induced electromotive force in the coil.
Explain why the magnetic flux linked with a coil changes when it is rotated in a uniform magnetic field with angular velocity omega.
Derive the expression for the instantaneous EMF E = NBA omega sin(omega t) induced in a rotating rectangular coil in a uniform magnetic field from first principles.
State Lenz's law and explain why it is a direct consequence of the principle of conservation of energy.

A bar magnet falls vertically through a stationary copper ring with its north pole pointing downwards. Predict the direction of induced current viewed from above as the magnet approaches and as it leaves.
Why does a metallic ring feel warm when a bar magnet is repeatedly thrust into and pulled out of it?
A rectangular loop moves with constant velocity into a region of uniform magnetic field perpendicular to the loop. Plot the induced current versus time.
Predict the polarity of the capacitor in a closed loop when the north pole of a magnet approaches one face and the south pole of another magnet approaches the opposite face simultaneously.
What are eddy currents? Mention two undesirable effects of eddy currents and explain how they are minimized in transformer cores.
Explain the principle of electromagnetic damping in a dead-beat moving coil galvanometer.
A copper plate is allowed to swing like a pendulum between the poles of a strong electromagnet. Why does it come to rest quickly when the magnet is turned on?
